origin.description: Extract several substrings from each string.
origin.usage: stri_sub_all(str, from = list(1L), to = list(-1L), length, use_matrix = TRUE, ignore_negative_length = TRUE)

arguments.name: from
arguments.text: A list of integer vectors, or one vector that is wrapped into a list. A list of two-column matrices is accepted when use_matrix is TRUE.

arguments.name: to
arguments.text: A list of inclusive end indexes. A plain vector is wrapped into a list.

arguments.name: length
arguments.text: A list of lengths. When passed, to is ignored.

arguments.name: use_matrix
arguments.text: Passed through to each stri_sub call. A single TRUE reads matrix indexes.

arguments.name: ignore_negative_length
arguments.text: When TRUE, the default, a negative length is dropped from that string's pieces instead of becoming NA.

origin.details: The i-th result is stri_sub(str[i], from[[i]], to[[i]]), with recycling when the list lengths differ. A vector that is not a list is wrapped first, so one index vector is applied to every string.

translation.description: Extract several substrings from each string.
translation.usage: stri_sub_all(str, from_=None, to=None, length=None, use_matrix=True, ignore_negative_length=True)

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A string, or a list of strings. Missing entries are stringi._na.NA.

arguments.name: from_
arguments.text: Indexes. This is from in R. A flat list is one index vector shared across strings. A list of lists gives each string its own indexes. IndexMatrix, or a dict of two columns, is one matrix.

arguments.name: to
arguments.text: End indexes, with the same list shape as from_.

arguments.name: length
arguments.text: Lengths. When passed, to is ignored.

arguments.name: use_matrix
arguments.text: Coerced as a single logical value. 1 is TRUE. NA is an error when any string is processed.

arguments.name: ignore_negative_length
arguments.text: When True, the default, a negative length is omitted from that string's pieces.

translation.details: Each string is sliced with stri_sub. A flat index vector is wrapped into one list element and recycled. A negative length is dropped, which is the opposite of stri_sub, where that length becomes NA.
translation.value: A list of lists of strings.
translation.example:
from stringi.sub import stri_sub_all
print(stri_sub_all("a b c", from_=[1, 3, 5], to=[1, 3, 5]))
